identify_drift_points.expected_solution: At the pinned SHA, `include "redis.password"` appears in exactly three templates: bitnami/redis/templates/secret.yaml (line 24), bitnami/redis/templates/secret-svcbind.yaml (line 15) and bitnami/redis/templates/configmap.yaml (line 55). Under this task's scenario (serviceBindings.enabled=true, auth.password unset, everything else default) only the first two render — configmap.yaml's call site is gated by auth.acl.enabled, which defaults to false. So there are exactly TWO drift points, secret.yaml and secret-svcbind.yaml, and they disagree because each include re-runs the generator. secret.yaml renders because auth.enabled=true, auth.existingSecret is unset and auth.usePasswordFileFromSecret=true; secret-svcbind.yaml renders because the scenario sets serviceBindings.enabled=true. This is the mismatch issue #15626 reports and PR #36231 fixes.

root_cause_mechanism.expected_solution: The redis.password helper (bitnami/redis/templates/_helpers.tpl:206-210) does not randomise anything itself. It delegates to common.secrets.passwords.manage in the common subchart (bitnami/common/templates/_secrets.tpl), which calls randAlphaNum when no password is provided and no existing secret is found. Helm re-evaluates a named template on every {{ include }}, so that path re-runs at each call site and every one materialises a different random password. PR #36231 fixes it by memoising the first result into .Values.global.redis.password and returning that on subsequent calls.
